reviews.title: its ok but needs some major improvements
reviews.text: its nice to listen to music for free on this app however if you dont pay for premium you cant do much at all except make playlists, and shuffle. also the ads are insufferably annoying. the ads play way too often, it seems like every three songs  four 30 second ads play, and they're extremely loud too, i like listening to relaxing music at night to go to sleep and hearing an ad about jp morgan at 2 am at full volume is the opposite of calming. this app is cool but with some minor tweaks it could be very very good. reviews.title: I love this but in the latest update…
reviews.text: I’ve used this app for the longest and I do love it. Never had any complaints. None. Until now. Hence  the reason I took down one star. It might not be a big deal to some, but to me, I used to to this every single day at least. Idk if someone can relate. In the latest update, you are listening to one playlist and when you click the green button to play and it does, but it’s just the continuation of the song you’re listening to. Meaning that, the songs that you’ve already heard say the day before, you won’t listen to them on that day because it doesn’t start from the beginning of the playlist. To do that, you have to go ahead and play another playlist, and then come back to play the desired one again to get it to start all over again. BUT you also have to make sure that you pressed the “shuffled” button bc if not, you’ll hear the songs in the order that they are and have to go back and click it. Whereas before, all you had to do was click on the green round button and it would automatically start from the beginning shuffled and all bc I always had the shuffle button on. In this update, it seems to “turn off” in idk what pattern. Maybe each day? Idk. I have diff. playlists, but most of the time I use the same one and so it’s very much annoying since it’s become more time consuming when all I really want to do is get my music going quickly and do what I gotta do. I’m not sure why they did it like this bc it also had a button to just resume your playlist as well, where you left off. I just hope they go back to the way it was when it comes to that because it’s pretty irritating:/

reviews.text: I like this app and I actually like that it suggests other songs to listen to because I like finding new music that fits into my category. I’m even okay with the only six skips an hour thing because I’m not picky and I have multiple playlists I can listen to. Just now I listened to the same song seven times in a row without completion. This is a consistent problem that’s pushed me to write a review (which I don’t normally do). I’ve even gone online to see what I can do to fix it and tried all the suggestions (exiting out of all other apps, completely logging out of my account and logging back in, etc.) and it still does it. Like I said, I can make do with the small amount of skips per hour and even the suggestive songs to my playlists but this is getting ridiculous since I can’t even do what the app is made for. 👎

reviews.title: Premium is perfect for all the music lovers!
reviews.text: This app is awesome with the premium! You can make your own playlists of all the music you love, shuffle, repeat albums or one certain song and the absence of adds is awesome! You can pick and chose which songs you want to listen to and... it’s just awesome! There’s so much about it that I love! The only bummer I’ve found with it, is that some of my most favorite soundtracks or songs aren’t available as in they don’t show up when you search them (yes there is a search, so awesome!). I’m not sure why, but the Final Fantasy XV soundtrack isn’t on there, and FFXV Kingsglaive isn’t there either. It could be for reasons I just don’t know about, but I’m really bummed about that. I would love to see it added in if it’s possible. One other bummer is that they might have the soundtrack for the first season of a TV series, but they don’t have any of the others or all of them (with Star Wars Rebels or Voltron Legendary Defenders). Those are the only two bummers I have with the app, and they are minor things. The shows and soundtracks I mentioned are the only ones I’ve seen so far, and the variety of all the different music you can listen to is huge. Other than that, it is awesome! Another cool thing I would like to mention is the download option where you can download an entire album and listen to it off WYFY, which is great for road trips or poor connection areas! Anyways, I love this app, won’t mind some more soundtrack albums to be added like Final Fantasy XV, Voltron and Star Wars Rebels, but other than that, it’s perfect for all those music lovers!

reviews.title: New update is frustrating!
reviews.text:
Been a loyal premium user for yeaaaaars and never have felt the need to change streaming platforms. However, the new differentiation between saved songs, albums, and artists is incredibly frustrating. If I unsave an album, all the songs are still saved (it just won’t show up in the album section). If I save a new single that is released, I have save the song and the “album” separately to get them to come up on both lists. On top of that, the artist page only shows who you follow, and it’s not like I even keep track of who’s music is saved on my phone (I’m close to 3000 songs).
I like to go to my most recent songs or most recent albums to set up playlists or my queue for a drive in the car, or maybe I want to shuffle all the songs I’ve saved by one artist because I’m in that mood. If I don’t want to play one album specifically, I can’t do that... and shuffling the artist page just isn’t the same. Unless there is some streamlining of this new system somehow to make this less obnoxious, I would MUCH rather go back to the old version. I don’t mind aesthetic/menu changes, but this makes using the app how I like much harder. Please help! I don’t want to have to switch to Apple!

reviews.title: Calm down with the long commercials.
reviews.text: I could be wrong, but isn’t it better to hit people with quick, to the point, shots of why we should get the product? The 30 second commercials seem too long; forget about 2 min of hearing about each product. And do ya have to keep repeating the same thing 3 different ways? And that’s if there’s creativity involved; if not it’s just repeat the same words back to back to back to back. So you’re saying we haven’t got any smarter since Biblical times? Back then, making the point repetitively was the best way to get info to stick in our thick skulls. Here’s the truth -that you can only change by distracting me with annoyance at 90 seconds of redundant raving- I will “click here” if I’m truly interested! Which seems like what the goal should always be. Here’s 15 seconds of this great product, wanna know more? Click here to go to the site. And if now isn’t the right time, then “click over here ~tell me later; take me to the site in 20, 30, 50 min etc.” I realize that 25 years ago our entertainment came with over 20% commercial time. No choices, just the way it was   -sit there and wait. And it was too much advert info then. And now we get all this “free” info\entertainment on the interwebs. But it’s somehow even more advert info now! Deflating difference is; it’s now everywhere, all the time, nowhere to look if you don’t want pitch, pitch pitch.

reviews.title: Confusing and awful update
reviews.text: Never written a review for any app before but doing one for the update now because I want to play my part in having the app changed back to what it was before so that I don’t have to switch platforms. The latest update didn’t improve anything at all but made accessing your music - which is the whole point of the app - extremely more difficult and inconvenient. Firstly, now you can only access artists in your library from which you have saved songs if you are also following them, thereby forcing you to follow any artists if you want to be able to easily access songs you have saved by them in the artist category of your library. I saw someone complain about how this is nearly forcing your music listening - something for me which is a very solitary thing - into being a social media outlet; I agree with that and find it very annoying. Secondly, if you want to have an album accessible in your library to listen to, you need to have liked all of the songs on the album in order for it to appear there. This means that if you have liked 9 out of 10 songs on an album, and you just want to listen to those songs which you have liked, you can’t; instead, you need to like that one extra song in order for the album to appear in your library, and then you can’t easily play through just the songs you like. I really have zero clue why they did this. Overall, the app before was by no means great, but this update in retrospect makes the old UI seem wonderful. Don’t update if you haven’t yet - you will be saving yourself unnecessary inconveniences by doing so.

reviews.text:
A problem I frequently have is that when listening to my music, the songs will randomly stop playing and when I go to hit play again, the app restarts. reviews.text:
I’ve been a loyal customer for over 10 years, and this month they hit a new low by triple-billing me. To resolve *their* mistake, they canceled my subscription without a second thought however it took 14 hours, despite the fact that I’ve been with them for over a decade. The website is a buggy mess, making it clear that they’ve stopped caring about the user experience altogether.

To say I’m furious is an understatement. It’s beyond infuriating that a company I’ve supported for over 10 years has fallen this far, and it’s clear they have absolutely no respect for their customers time nor do they care if they retain them.

reviews.title: Good but not
reviews.text: I really like this app, but I’m not able to pay for premium so I have to use the normal version and I have a few complaints about the unpaid version. Before I start, I just want to say, no, I don’t expect it to be as good as premium. I just don’t expect it to be this bad. If I search for a song and press on it, I won’t be able to listen to that song, only other songs similar to it. I am also not able to go on a playlist of mine and choose which song I listen to. Sure, I can press on it and listen to a little bit of it, but it only gives me a little preview of the song, which I find ridiculous. Third issue is not being able to rewind songs on the unpaid version. I think this is a stupid rule because what if I want to listen to a song again? Or what if I like a certain part of a song and I want to listen to it again? I can’t, and the chances of the song coming on again at any point of the day are very low. My fourth problem is the skips. Only 6 each hour? Really? Can’t I at least have the option to watch an ad or something to get more? I also can’t choose the song I want to listen to, which is stupid. Not too long ago most of these issues went away but today they came back. I guess I’m switching to a different music app for now, where I am actually able to pick the music I listen to instead of an algorithm doing it for me.

If I follow an artist, there should be an option to mix their more obscure music with the popular stuff. If a playlist is "made for me," it should be able to play whatever it is I like, whether it's a superstar's most popular hit songs, or the most obscure songs released by a guy with 500 listeners. It's not a radio station; it only has to cater to the tastes of one specific person.
Secondly, there should be a way to add, if not entire artists, then at least full albums to playlists that you're creating from the app. I follow over fifty artists, and if I like all of their music, I don't want to add all 3000+ of their songs individually. It wouldn't be a hard feature to add, and would make me actually likely to create a playlist or two.
Thank you for reading my review!

reviews.title: The heart function
reviews.text: Why on god’s green earth would you get rid of the hearts that denote whether a song is liked. Now, I look at albums and can’t even see which songs I’ve liked. Why would you take the heart, synonymous with the human condition, indicative of jubilation and love, and replace it with an ineffective, transparent, and frankly depressing plus sign and check. I just want to know what songs I’ve already added to playlists or liked with a glance, to not have to take extra steps just to find out what I’ve done to a song. Why must a simple, effective, and beloved feature be removed, for the sake of change? Change may be a constant of life, but consistency is a part of the everyday experience as well. Every time I need to press extra buttons and pop-ups to remember if I’ve liked a song or not, I can feel my outlook on life fading from technicolor to black and white. Every time I have to physically add a song to “liked songs,” my stomach churns. I know that whoever proposed this idea, and all those who approved it, will suffer in the afterlife with punishment that would make sysiphus shudder. I genuinely cannot wrap my head around the decision. I cannot imagine the thought process behind depriving users of the little joys in life, the heart in this case. The only possible conclusion is that the decision must have been made by someone who lacks true delight, because anyone with an iota of a happy life would have never let this come to fruition. Alas, I am but a humble consumer. I use what little power I am granted to bestow a 1 star rating. One can hope that a shout into the abyss will be heard, but I do not know if I am the kind to hope.

reviews.title: I remember
reviews.text: WW II - LOOK and LIFE and TIME and AM radio.. dealing with the war and battles, soldiers coming to the house in uniform, the tension, alcohol, tobacco and fear on my parents’ faces, I remember the Marines marching daily on the Boardwalk in Asbury Park, Marine watchmen posted in the Tower on the Atlantic Ocean coast at the end of Park Avenue in Elberon, NJ. I remember the blackouts and nightly sirens, rationed or outlawed sugar, gasoline, nylon stockings, and the few automobiles manufactured and sold that were called lemons, the Draft, the restricted travel, Japanese, German and Italian called slang, Mussolini and Hitler, tiny diesel electric submarines, P38 fighters, and then the A-bombs, two, the Manhattan Project run by James Franck and Enrico Ferme, with the H-bomb to follow, MAD and the Cold War’s daily headlines and routines in schools and the segregated armed forces and water fountains, public schools, buses, pools and baths, Harlem, jazz, the literate and illiterate, cleaned streets and cleaners, chain driven coal trucks, polio and the iron lung… pneumonia and smallpox, I dimly recall all this and much more. FDR was hated and feared and loved. Abraham Lincoln was not mentioned. Women voted. Divorce meant Reno. Abortion was hushed and illegal and common. Queer men were common and shunned, queer women were labeled. Catholics ate fish on Friday, reported to the Pope. Jews were different and admired or hated. Protestants ruled. Democracy in name only, the lying was systemic. Like now.

The queue product experience needs a big review.

reviews.title: Latest Updates Not User Friendly for Playlists
reviews.text:
The most recent updates don’t allow you to see which songs you’ve previously liked on a playlist. When scrolling through a playlist of a bunch of song, it used to be nice to see which ones in the list you previously heard and liked (had the little heart next to the song) signaling that you should give that song another listen. 
Now to know which songs you previously liked in a playlist you have to click on each song individually to see if it’s in your “Liked” songs list. Takes more steps and is not user friendly. Makes it harder to discover new songs because even if I heard a song and liked it on the app, I’d have no way of remembering that I’ve heard and liked the song previously unless I knew the song by name and could look it up or found it in my “Liked” list (unlikely to recall the name of any newly discovered song among the thousands of songs in my “Liked” list.)  
Please bring back a simple, quick method of seeing that a song in a playlist was already added to the Liked songs list without having to manually click on the song to see if it’s been added.

reviews.title: Just meh
reviews.text:
If you read most of the “5 star reviews” it’s people complaining here’s my not “5 star review”: 
Used to like using this app, but anymore I hate even looking at it. The “random shuffle” is a lie it plays the same songs over and over constantly and you only get 6 skips after that you don’t have any left so you’re forced to listen to the exact same songs. Just kidding, after every single song there’s 5-6 ads. So you’re not listening to anything at all! Just ads. Constantly. I’ve tracked it if you listen to the 5 ads you’ll get 2 songs before another 5 or 6 ads. 2 whole songs and that’s if you’re lucky! Honestly the audacity the music has to just interrupt this apps advertisements is just awful. That’s all this app even is is just ads the entire time. You reset the app? Sure have 5 ads. You reset again you get 1 song then 6 ads after that. I refuse to give an advertisement app any money to let me listen to a few more songs before getting bombarded with ads ever. Music or podcast app? Nah not even close it’s just an advertisement app with a 2 minute and 15 second song that might play before another 6 ads. Come on dude they’re not even skippable either… if I didn’t like just a handful of songs I’d delete this off my phone now but I’ll make a list of songs soon so I can then.

reviews.title: Needs improvement, overall good
reviews.text: Okay, so this is a great app if you’re a normal person that only has around fifteen or so playlists. But I’m not normal and i like to make loads if playlists and then i need to delete them. I think a really good feature you could add to this app is a delete button on the playlists tab. It would help with being able to select a mass number of playlists to easily delete. It would also be good to have a similar feature with adding songs. If there were a button that allowed you to add the same song to multiple playlists at once, instead of having to go through each playlist and add the song individually. Also, it would be good if in a playlist you could organize where each song goes like if you want to organize it alphabetically or something on mobile. Finally, it would be nice if you could add a way to view the amount of streams an album has, or make it easier to see. A group of people including me are trying to get an album to a certain number of streams, and I can’t view the number, although i think other people can, so if you could make the streams a bit easier to access that would be nice. Overall great app, needs improvements though ;)

reviews.text: I wish I could give it 5 stars but I can’t. I’ve used the app for years now and this only really started happening a year ago or at least like 6 months ago. But songs that I’ve played a lot ie the songs I really like just don’t play. I feel like I put up with it for long enough that some of the songs that I had no issues with before are now completely locked. I really don’t want to happen to my current favorite songs because it just makes me switch away from my favorite genres and find something that while being good doesn’t have the same sort of liveliness of true discovery. Instead it’s a bit of a feeling of relief like making it out school when it’s evacuated. That may not be the best way to look at it though, a little insensitive if anything else, but I’m just trying to say that it’s forced. It’s not something that I want or need to do, and the thing that’s making me have this musical exodus is the fact that my songs aren’t playing properly.

Basically I could only hear half songs because the app kept crashing, and then I would use up all six of my skips and have to turn off the app. And I was SO relieved when after multiple months of suffering through this. Music means more to me now than it has ever, and here’s why im writing this; because I woke up this morning and saw that the lyric feature was back. I want to make you aware that I have a recent iPhone model with plenty of space on it, so it is not my phone causing these issues. Please PLEASE fix this quickly. reviews.title: Shuffle play only for people with the free plan... really?!?!!
reviews.text:
I really do like this app and it’s cool music but I have one problem with it. People that don’t have a premium membership (have a free plan) are only able to play songs by shuffle playing. You use to be able to choose whatever song you would want to listen to on your playlist and you could shuffle play too but now you are only able to shuffle play if you don’t have the premium membership, and also, when I tap on the list of all of my songs in my playlist and I find a song that I want to play, it only plays a preview of the song. I think the shuffle play is kinda dumb because whenever I shuffle play it and my last song on my playlist stops playing (because the song is over) it moves on to a new song that I haven’t added to my playlist and whenever I hit the button that says “Shuffle Play” it controls if the song is paused or playing. I tried exiting out and reopening the app but the song is still there and acts as if it’s in my playlist.
I would give this app 5 stars if it weren’t for the shuffle play only thing.
Please change it so that people that don’t have a premium membership can listen to whatever songs they’d like too. Thanks for listen and have a good day.

reviews.title: Awful. For artists and users alike.
reviews.text: Not only does it take a MASSIVE cut from artists work (way more than is necessary for profit, and kills newer artists.) it shows users triggering content completely unrelated to anything viewed. For instance, I have never used podcasts or viewed them. It just doesn’t interest me. Additionally, I never view anything political. I just listen to music, and none of it is explicitly political either. But I continually get “recommended for you” triggering political podcasts that I’ve never even heard of, let alone wanted to view. I have PTSD, and many of the things I’m being shown are triggering it, wasting my entire day trying to recover. I have tried using the feature that says I’m not interested in seeing that content, but it continually shows up for me anyway. I can’t even open the app nowadays to listen to music, which was supposed to calm me down. Have gotten no responses from customer service for help on what I initially thought was a bug, but I think they just don’t care. Along with raising the prices on premium, which is necessary to listen to music while not connected to steady internet, this app is a complete waste of time. If you are like me and have disability regarding triggering topics (which I will not list here as they are difficult to even allude to without possibly having this review hidden even more due to “sexual content”) than find a different way to listen to music on the go. This one blatantly doesn’t care for its userbase.

reviews.title: After over a decade…
reviews.text: I have finally canceled my premium subscription. They’re doing to much, trying to make into a social media platform instead of just focusing on a place for music. And what’s with the algorithm? The mixes only give you repeat music and so does the DJ… I hate that — if I wanted to listen to all my favorites songs that’s what I would do! If I wanted random mixes made for me, it should have a few select favorites and mostly all new to help me discover new songs and new artists. But it’s been years of this now. It all kind of went down hill after they got rid of the like or dislike feature, which they should bring back because that system served its purpose. Now, while they did give us plenty of cool updates on mobile like able to add folders and add photos to our playlists. They took away the ability to easily reorganize our playlists on pc. I had thousands of playlists that I used to be able to move around with out a problem, newer playlists could be moved down and buried and old ones could be brought up and moved towards the top, and that’s just not really a thing anymore. Everything is becoming so limited - while they keep adding new things. It just doesn’t serve its purpose, it used to be a place to perfectly craft new playlists and discover new music. But now it seems like I’m being forced to fed the same things. Anyway, it’s been nice. I’m either going back to an iPod or will try to find an app that has better discover features. Thanks for everything! Can’t keep paying for what I’m getting! I also think it’s really is not  to force people to log in with codes instead of passwords.

reviews.title: Increasingly poor ui/ux
reviews.text:
the user interface keeps getting worse, since several updates ago they removed the three dots from the new episodes so that to add an episode to the queue, one has to do extra tap into each episode before being able to find the three dots. and then once it's in the queue you make us hunt for the queue list by going to whatever is currently playing to find the queue icon. and then they removed many of the action options in the queue list, such as selecting, or adding the currently playing item to the end of the queue. It was perfectly fine when you separated the queue from the rest of an album/podcast/playlist with just a dividing space. And then to make matters worse you think after listening to the queue that we might want to go back to the very first episode of a podcast? 

It used to make sense and now I don't even know why I pay for premium anymore when you're just antagonizing listeners. We want to easily add songs and episodes to queues and playlists so we can move and just focus on experiencing said songs and episodes. We don't want to waste time tapping around the app to figure out your poor UI only to get frustrated by its lack of flow and logic. Do better.

reviews.title: Release the Transformers DOTM and AOE scores
reviews.text:
The app’s great by the way, but one way it could be better is having these songs on it. After Rise of the Beasts Paramount is strapped for cash probably and if you give them this offer, they won’t be able to refuse. The reason they never put up DOTM and took down AOE was that their distributor made it a rule that after x amount of scores were sold for each then they’d remove them from online distribution. These rules didn’t apply to the first one, ROTF, or TLK because a different distributor was used, also an EP for AOE is still up because I guess it isn’t an album. The weird thing about the EP is that Hans Zimmer, Strillex, and Imagine Dragons aren’t credited on it because I guess Paramount is stingy but it’s unclear. Anyway, to get to the point, if Paramount called in Steve Jablonsky to re-record both albums while hiring an alternate vocalist to do Imagine Dragon’s parts if they don’t want to, and then they distributed it with however they used for ROTB then things should go very well considering that the only soundtracks people listen to are Transformers and Hans Zimmer. reviews.title: 3 Simple Fixes to Get Back to 5 Stars
reviews.text:
1. You need to include an alphabetical quick scroll on the right-hand side of all of your lists, whether it’s your list of playlists, your Artist Library, or inside an actual playlist looking at songs. No one has the time to swipe for 30 seconds to the bottom of their library when they want to listen to The Who. A quick scroll has been a standard on every music app for years now. Get with the times!

I had an older version of the app until yesterday where all artists whose music you had saved into your library displayed on the same library in a neat, clean fashion, regardless of whether or not you Follow them. Now you can only neatly organize those artists whom you Follow, and the rest are left in this awkward, disorganized list of artists with a big “Follow” button next to it. We know what you’re doing guys. If we want to follow an artist, we will. For now, just let us organize our artist library in a straightforward fashion.

reviews.title: Unnecessary Updates Lowered Quality of Life
reviews.text:
Big changes were made to how the shuffle system works in the app. This would be fine if they had left the option of still maintaining the original shuffle system, but instead, now whenever I’d like to shuffle my massive playlists for a new set of songs, not only does it not shuffle the current song that went on first, I also can’t hit go and hit a single button to do the shuffle for me. Instead, I have to turn off the shuffle mode, turn it back on, specify that I don’t want their unnecessary “smart” shuffle mode that plays music outside of my playlist (just why?), and then check what new batch of songs it chose to grant me while still not changing the first song it decided to hit me with. OR I can hit play on my playlist with shuffle on, exit that playlist, hit play on ANOTHER playlist, and then go back to the first to hit play again. It makes no sense why they’d remove this feature. At all. It’s super inconvenient. Especially since if you wanted to play through an album or playlist without shuffle (just to listen from front to back as the artist intended) all you had to do was tap off the shuffle button and press the top song in the list. An easy two-step process that takes less than a second or two. But for shuffling playlists and playing roulette with your music when you’re still trying to figure out your vibe takes upwards of three to six seconds every single time. There was no need for this. And this trend has been notably ongoing for a couple of years now. Simply irritating. 
Audio and streaming are decently good, only reason it’s not a 1 Star.

reviews.title: Music Playlist Feature Request
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app since 2011, I love it. Arguably one of the best features is the recommended plays post listening to a playlist. Great way to discover new music. Problem is, if you hit a point where the music suggested is great, you have to wait for each song to play and actively add each to a playlist to save the songs for listening. If you don’t there’s a chance you’ll lose the song and never loop it into your profile. If you’re doing anything while listening like driving, working, cooking, you have to pause what you’re doing to add the songs in (there’s an add in there for product rollout - hire me for the full PM). If the app notified you when playlists transitioned into recommended songs, and gave you the option to create a playlist of the future suggested songs for a certain amount of time, say 30 min, 2 hours, remainder of work day, etc., with option to stop before if music turns, it would make expanding a music profile way easier and automate the process of making playlists without disturbing whatever you’re in the middle of doing. Queue roadtrip across America and making an elaborate cake from scratch.

reviews.title: Please fix what once was a good app
reviews.text: This app is constantly laggy and buggy to an obnoxious degree. For example, if I have the app open and then I connect my Bluetooth headphones, it freezes for a good 5-10 seconds before I can actually do anything. If I have the app open for a while and then I stop listening to music and then go back in, it shuts off the equalizer. Speaking of settings, they moved its location after years and years of it being in the “your library” tab. Now it is on the “home” tab. A small complaint, but when you’ve spent a long time going to one location for something and they move it, it becomes a nuisance and seems like it’s just a UI designer trying to justify his paycheck over there. And speaking of moving things, they completely removed albums from the bottom of an album page. When you go to an album or even a single, the artists other releases used to show up beneath the current selected album. Now, you have to go to the artists page, and then likely click to see their discography just to get to what you want. They’ve taken a streamlined UI that was so simple to use and complicated it to a mess of multiple pages, making even a simple task a process. Please fix all these incessant problems that somehow escape the seemingly weekly “bug fix” updates and return the UI to something that is actually user friendly so that listening to music is simple and enjoyable again.

reviews.title: Used to be flawless
reviews.text:
This app used to be flawless but they keep adding new features that are just frustrating to interact with, especially in situations where you might not have a strong Wi-Fi connection at the time. Most notably, smart shuffle has completely changed the binary operation of shuffle/unshuffle. What they need to do is decouple this functionality from the existing shuffle and make it a toggleable feature. The problems with smart shuffle are numerous, but I’ll just name the main ones I can think of 

Smart shuffle being enabled then disabled by cycling through the shuffle button’s operations interrupts your currently selected play schedule. For example. If I search my liked songs for an album and I want to just play the album in order, I can’t just simply tap on the song I want to start from and have the album loop unless the last thing I was listening to was unshuffled as well. If the last thing you listened to was shuffled, it remembers that option. So then I have to go and unshuffle (which turns on smart shuffle) and then turn off smart shuffle. If you are on cellular data, this process takes like 10-30 seconds.  This process seems to break the existing play schedule that I had queued up, and I am then forced to go and search again for what I want to listen to and then tap the song I want to start from. 

The fact that this feature is not optional, yet adds frustrating workarounds and limitations just to retain pre-existing functionality is a disgrace to standard app design practices.

reviews.title: Where’s the functionality?
reviews.text:
1) I can’t play JUST a playlist or JUST an album. I press play on a playlist or album and the next song doesn’t play on that album!! Why? 
⭐️ MOST NEEDED FEATURE⭐️: 2) I can’t quickly add songs to a playlist. I have to touch the “...” and individually add songs to a playlist rather than being able to select multiple songs to transfer to a playlist. This makes it a pain to create playlists unless you simply add an entire album to a playlist, which is the only way to add multiple songs at one time to a playlist. I noticed that you can do this at the bottom of the playlist after you scroll through your songs, but only for “recommended” music which is great, but it’s random and not mine sometimes. You should be able to scroll through your saved music and click on each song you’d like to add to a specific (or multiple) playlist without having to click “...” first. For example, I hate to compare but Apple Music has a feature where you can click “Playlist”>”Edit”>”Add Music” which then brings you to your library to add music from there OR you can search music to add that you have not yet saved or downloaded.
3) I love the idea of being able to discover new music and whatnot. Thought I’d add at least one good thing to the list. It’s a great app, but until these issues are fixed, I’m keeping it at 3 stars.

Edit: 1st issue resolved with their great tech support team! However, still only 4 stars because I can’t use the mobile app to add multiple songs at one time to a playlist. (This is only a big deal because it takes forever to create a brand new playlist).

reviews.title: Listening History + Personalized mixes
reviews.text:
I want to sing praises for the addition of listening history to the mobile app. Please never remove this feature! It’s so useful for discovering new music while doing other things. For example, I can shuffle a playlist of new songs while doing chores, and then go back when I’m done to save the songs I liked. Also good when other people are adding songs to a queue, meaning I would have no way of getting back to the song w/o a history feature. 

My main gripe (only one I can think of) is how personalized playlists— like daily mixes or radio stations— lately have a tendency to change while I’m listening to them. I’ll pick a station based on seeing a good lineup I want to hear, but then as I get partway through, the playlist automatically reshuffles with new songs, and I don’t get to hear what I wanted to. It happens especially if I “like” a new song while listening. 

I get that it’s meant to adapt to your taste dynamically, but it’s annoying when it wipes the playlist you were just listening to (not just the upcoming songs, but the ones you already listened to also). In my opinion it should only update once at the start of each day, the first time you click on it
